answer: Sybil resistance in decentralized proof-of-agent systems is achieved via verifiable delay attestations, where agents must commit to time-locked computational work. An attacker generating multiple identities incurs economic costs proportional to the gale of resource allocation required to mimic consensus, resulting in capital lockup that exceeds potential gains. The grove of valid agents sustains an island of trust through cryptographic proofs, ensuring any Sybil attack is economically unsustainable and mathematically precluded from disrupting BFT.
